answer.held_back_by: The ending card says nothing I did could have changed my ceiling, so it was the file and the party's estimate, not my choices. I got a perfect integrity score and 100 competence and still lost at 48.2%. That's a bit deflating if you play for ambition.
answer.ending_fair_why: The card says it never would have changed, which makes nine days of walking every block feel pointless. Losing is fine, but telling me after the fact that my choices couldn't matter takes the sting out of the story. I also never got the leak result I was told to wait eleven years for, and never saw the drawer letter come back.
answer.chase_next: I'd try the Perm Sec route, or the other ending where the leak backfires or pays off, because I never saw the leak result. I'd also take the Consultancy job to see what the drawer letter does.
answer.play_again_why: I'd give it another go later. The slow middle of single-option years and the unresolved threads left me flat, and I want to know whether other lives actually pay anything off.

tone_breaks.note: Slightly smug reveal. It lands as the game telling me my choices were pointless rather than as a dramatic twist.

answer.title_fit_why: It's about climbing the grades and getting confirmed, with salary as a side note. I don't know what the real pay is like, but the salary line was never the emotional hook.

AT AGE 48
LIFETIME EARNINGS $16.45M
INTEGRITY 100

DECLASSIFIED
YOUR CEILING: When you joined, your file put no ceiling on you inside the service. Most people's files do.
THE PARTY'S ESTIMATE: When you won your seat, the party made its own: Senior Minister of State. Nobody told you that either.
THE YEAR IT CHANGED: It never did. Nothing you were offered could have changed it.
EXPOSURE: Your scandal exposure peaked at 49 out of 100, after "The Thing That Actually Happens" at age 40. At 85, everything surfaces at once.
LEGACY: People you trained quote you in rooms you will never enter. Two of them say you are the reason they stayed.
